en: *Samvarodayatantra*, Chapter 11: The Chapter on the Instruction for the Rules of Mantra Recitation Now, therefore, I shall explain the secret characteristic of mantra recitation. One should first draw the mandala, and afterwards [visualize] oneself as the deity. (11.1) In mountain caves, thickets, and groves, on the shores of the great ocean, at crossroads, in pavilions, or in delightful cremation grounds; (11.2) One should properly perform the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*) according to the previously stated rules. One who knows the heart-mantra should recite it on a mountain or in a mountain location. (11.3) *Oṃ śrī heruka hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. One should recite it one hundred thousand times, or perform the fire-oblation (*homayet*) with a tenth part of that amount. Mundane and supramundane accomplishments (*siddhi*) will arise quickly; it is not otherwise. (11.4) In a thicket dense with trees, one should always draw the mandala. One should accomplish the mantra by severing it with the weapon-mantra (*astra*), and always recite the "heart-with-heart" (*m-upahṛda*). (11.5) *Oṃ hrīḥ ha ha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. One should recite this up to three hundred thousand times, and perform the fire-oblation with a tenth part of that amount. One should accomplish the bringing of rain, the neutralizing of poisons, and the accomplishment of speech (*vāksiddhi*). (11.6) In a place with clear water, one should draw an auspicious mandala. One should recite the mantra without interruption, having performed the recitation of the face-mantra (*mukhamantra*). (11.7) *Oṃ sumbhani sumbhani hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | gṛhṇa 2 hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | gṛhṇāpaya 2 hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | ānaya hoḥ vidyārāja hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. The yogin should recite four hundred thousand times and perform the fire-oblation with a tenth part of that amount. He accomplishes pacification (*śānti*), enrichment (*puṣṭi*), subjugation (*vaśya*), and the accomplishment of the welfare of sentient beings. (11.8) Having gone to the shore of the great ocean, one should draw the mandala. One should especially recite the goddess-mantra three hundred thousand times. (11.9) Completing the procedure as stated, one should perform the fire-oblation with a tenth part of that amount. *Oṃ vajravairocanīye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. (11.10) All mundane accomplishments and even the accomplishment of the *khecarī* [flight] are attained. Having drawn the mandala in a cremation ground, one who knows the previously stated rules (11.11) Should accomplish the seven-syllable mantra, reciting it exactly three hundred thousand times. Performing the fire-oblation with a tenth part, he should accomplish the rite with complete certainty. (11.12) The rites of causing hatred, expulsion, and especially killing, succeed through mere recitation, according to the word of Vajrasattva. (11.13) Having drawn the mandala at a crossroads, one should accomplish the rite of immobilization (*stambhana*). By reciting the *ḍākinī*-mantra ten thousand times, it is accomplished. (11.14) *Oṃ ḍākinīye hūṃ 2 phaṭ*. Performing the fire-oblation with a tenth part, there is accomplishment in the subduing of spirits (*bhūta-vyatāda*). In a monastery or a pavilion, one should draw the excellent mandala. (11.15) One should recite the *lāmā*-mantra exactly one hundred thousand times. Performing the fire-oblation with a tenth part, the goddess is accomplished; there is no doubt in this. (11.16) *Oṃ lāme hūṃ 2 phaṭ*. One should always draw the mandala in a delightful, secluded place for the sake of collyrium, foot-ointment, and subjugation. One should accomplish the mantra of Khaṇḍarohā and others according to the rules. (11.17) *Oṃ khaṇḍarohe hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. One should recite two hundred thousand times and perform the fire-oblation with a tenth part. One should recite the mantra without interruption to accomplish the *yakṣas* and *yakṣiṇīs*. (11.18) Having prepared flowers, incense, perfumes, offerings, and especially food and drink, and having made the excellent mandala, (11.19) One should recite the *rūpiṇī*-mantra exactly six hundred thousand times. Performing the fire-oblation with a tenth part, O Goddess, she is accomplished; there is no doubt in this. (11.20) *Oṃ rūpiṇīye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. With special songs and dances, and sounding the mantra of the mudrās, one should accomplish [the rite] during a festival when the occasion has arrived, in suitable locations. (11.21) One should observe the color and other attributes of whichever specific rite is to be performed. The seat is the form of the deity, and the flower-offering is according to the rule. (11.22) When it is time for the preliminary service, one should maintain silence there. One should accomplish the power of the mantra, provided with the *mali-bali* offering. (11.23) One should observe the number there as a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred thousand. Through the recitation of countless mantras, one brings about supreme virtue. By the application of their rules, one should accomplish and attain success (*siddhi*). (11.24) Thus ends the eleventh chapter, the instruction on the rules for mantra recitation.
